children: having just reported fiscal third-quarter results that showed one in four dollars of revenue coming from the major hyperscalers, investment firm Needham believes the fragility between the semiconductor giant and the hyperscalers is going both ways.

“Nearly one in every four dollars of [hyperscaler capital spending became Nvidia] revenue in the most recent quarter, we estimate,” Needham analyst Laura Martin wrote in a note to clients. “Hyperscaler dependence on NVDA remained at ~24% in the Sept/Oct quarter (flat q/q), its 2-year low. Hyperscaler dependence on NVDA peaked in the December 2025 quarter, at 32%, and has fallen since then. Structurally high co-dependence suggests a fragility that adds risks to the hyperscalers we cover (AMZN, GOOGL, META), especially with the management transition going on at NVDA.”
Delving deeper, Martin said the hyperscalers, a group of companies defined as Amazon

, have seen their capital spending soar. Over the past seven quarters, hyperscaler capital spending has risen roughly three times to approximately $251B. SpaceX has seen the fastest growth, up 376% year-over-year to $20B in its most recent quarter, followed by Amazon (up 209%), Google (up 200%), Meta (up 170%), and Microsoft (up 135%).

“Since NVDA's share of hyperscaler [capital spending] is falling over time, this implies that the hyperscalers are spending more CapX on other components of the AI value chain, at least in the near term,” Martin added.

title: Amazon, Google, Meta in spotlight as Needham sees 'fragility' due to Nvidia dependence
